```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 10)
```


```{r}
source("setup.R")
```

First, we load in the water supply database. We are only performing this rapid assessment on CONUS water supplies that are not municipal or hauled water supplies.

```{r}
water_supplies <- read_excel("data/Water_Supply_Systems/NPS_Water_Systems_Database_Joined_KW_Copy.xlsx", sheet = 1, na = c("NA","U"), skip = 1) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  filter(!state %in% c("AK", "AS", "HI", "MP", "PR", "VI")) %>%
  filter(!source_type %in% c("Municipal", "Hauled")) %>%
  mutate(source_longitude = as.numeric(source_longitude),
         source_latitude = as.numeric(source_latitude)) %>%
  drop_na(source_latitude, source_longitude) %>%
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = (c("source_longitude","source_latitude")),
               crs = 4326) %>%
  select(park_unit, wsd_source_id)
```

Next, we load in our list of MWBM rasters we want to use for our analyses. Currently, we are using all future climate scenarios contained within Alder's database, and the "training" historical data sent to us directly that is currently unavailable to the public.

```{r}
# list of all NetCDF runoff files
runoff_rasters <- list.files("data/all/loca2_mwbm/", full.names = TRUE, pattern = "*runoff") %>%
  .[!grepl("historical", .)]
```

Then, we calculate runoff vulnerability score. There are two components to the runoff indicator:

1) Runoff change "severity": this component is defined as the 10th percentile of projected runoff changes across all climate models for each water supply location. This 10th percentile value is then normalized using min-max scaling, where the minimum and maximum values across all locations are used to rescale the data to a 0-1 range (`maxmin_p10_percent_change`). 

2) "Consistency" of decreased runoff: this component is defined as the percentage of climate models that project negative runoff changes for each location and applies the same min-max normalization (maxmin_percent_models_negative). 

The final vulnerability score is computed as a weighted average of these two normalized components: 

`maxmin_recharge_vuln = (0.5 * maxmin_p10_percent_change) + (0.5 * maxmin_percent_models_negative)`

This approach gives equal weight to both the severity of the worst-case scenarios (10th percentile) and the consistency of negative projections across models, creating a composite vulnerability index that ranges from 0 to 1, where higher values indicate greater vulnerability to reduced runoff under future climate conditions.

```{r}
runoff_exp <- calc_runoff_exp(aoi = water_supplies,
                              runoff_data = runoff_rasters,
                              rerun_rast_extract = FALSE,
                              save = FALSE,
                              path = NULL)
```

### Model severity of [-] change in runoff: percentile score vs. normalized score

```{r, echo = FALSE}
runoff_exp <- runoff_exp %>%
  mutate(diff_p10 = maxmin_p10_percent_change - (pcntl_p10_percent_change/100),
         diff_negative = maxmin_percent_models_negative - (pcntl_percent_models_negative/100),
         diff_vuln = maxmin_recharge_vuln - (pcntl_recharge_vuln/100))

hist <- ggplot(runoff_exp, aes(x = raw_p10_percent_change)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "black", bins = 30) +
  labs(x = "Runoff Change (%)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

vs <- ggplot(runoff_exp, aes(x = pcntl_p10_percent_change, y = maxmin_p10_percent_change)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = raw_p10_percent_change), alpha = 0.7, color = "black", stroke = 0.5, shape = 21, size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("darkred", "pink", "green"),
                       values = scales::rescale(c(min(runoff_exp$raw_p10_percent_change, na.rm = TRUE),
                                                  0,
                                                  max(runoff_exp$raw_p10_percent_change, na.rm = TRUE))),
                       name = "Runoff Change (%)") +
  labs(x = "Percentiles",
       y = "Max-Min Normalized") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

dif <- ggplot(runoff_exp, aes(x = pcntl_p10_percent_change/100, y = diff_p10)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 3.5) +
  labs(x = "Percentiles", 
       y = "Difference (Max-Min - Percentiles)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

ggarrange(hist, vs, dif,  
          nrow = 1, 
          common.legend = TRUE,
          legend = "bottom",
          widths = c(1, 1.2, 1))
```

### Model consistency of [-] change in runoff: percentile score vs. normalized score

```{r, echo = FALSE}
hist <- ggplot(runoff_exp, aes(x = raw_percent_models_negative)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "black", bins = 30) +
  labs(x = "Negative Models (%)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

vs <- ggplot(runoff_exp, aes(x = pcntl_percent_models_negative, y = maxmin_percent_models_negative)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = raw_percent_models_negative), alpha = 0.7, color = "black", stroke = 0.5, shape = 21, size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("darkblue", "lightblue", "orange"),
                       name = "Negative Models (%)") +
  labs(#title = "Water Supply % Negative Models Rankings",
    x = "Percentiles",
    y = "Max-Min Normalized") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

dif <- ggplot(runoff_exp, aes(x = pcntl_percent_models_negative/100, y = diff_negative)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 3.5) +
  labs(x = "Percentiles", 
       y = "Difference (Max-Min - Percentiles)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

ggarrange(hist, vs, dif,  
          nrow = 1, 
          common.legend = TRUE,
          legend = "bottom",
          widths = c(1, 1.2, 1))
```

### Overall vulnerability: percentile score vs. normalized score

There appears to be several distinct vulnerability "pathways"; high runoff magnitude and consistency scores, low magnitude and consistency score, one where there's low magnitude but high consistency, and lastly where there's high magnitude but low consistency.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
hist <- ggplot(data = runoff_exp) +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = maxmin_recharge_vuln, fill = "Max-Min Normalized"), alpha = 0.4, bins = 30) +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = pcntl_recharge_vuln/100, fill = "Percentiles"), alpha = 0.3, bins = 30) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Max-Min Normalized" = "dodgerblue", "Percentiles" = "black")) +
  theme_bw() +
  xlab("Vulnerability Score") + ylab("Count") +
  labs(fill = "Method") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

vs <- ggplot(runoff_exp, aes(x = pcntl_recharge_vuln, y = maxmin_recharge_vuln)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = raw_p10_percent_change, size = raw_percent_models_negative), 
             alpha = 0.7, color = "black", stroke = 0.5, shape = 21) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("red", "yellow", "darkgreen"),
                       values = scales::rescale(c(min(runoff_exp$raw_p10_percent_change, na.rm = TRUE),
                                                  mean(runoff_exp$raw_p10_percent_change, na.rm = TRUE),
                                                  max(runoff_exp$raw_p10_percent_change, na.rm = TRUE))),
                       name = "Runoff (% change)") +
  scale_size_binned(name = "Negative Change Models (%)", 
                    range = c(0.01, 10),
                    n.breaks = 5,
                    breaks = c(0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100)) +
  labs(x = "Vulnerability Percentiles",
       y = "Vulnerability Max-Min Normalized") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

dif <- ggplot(runoff_exp, aes(x = pcntl_recharge_vuln/100, y = diff_vuln)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 3.5) +
  labs(x = "Percentiles", 
       y = "Difference (Max-Min - Percentiles)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

legend_hist <- get_legend(hist + theme(legend.position = "bottom"))
legend_vs <- get_legend(vs + theme(legend.position = "bottom"))

plots <- ggarrange(hist, vs, dif, nrow = 1, widths = c(1, 1.2, 1))

ggarrange(plots, 
          ggarrange(legend_hist, legend_vs, nrow = 1), 
          nrow = 2, heights = c(4, 1))
```
